name: Mohamed Mansour
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Mohamed Mansour oversees family conglomerate Mansour Group, which was founded by his father Loutfy (d. 1976) in 1952 and has 60,000 employees.
Mansour established General Motors dealerships in Egypt in 1975, later becoming one of GM's biggest distributors worldwide.
Mansour Group also has exclusive distribution rights for Caterpillar equipment in Egypt and seven other African countries.
Mansour, who has both Egyptian and U.K. citizenship, served as Egypt's minister of transportation from 2006 to 2009 under the Hosni Mubarak regime.
His brothers Yasseen and Youssef, who share ownership in the family group, are also billionaires; his son Loutfy heads private equity arm Man Capital.
forbes_facts: Mansour's father lost his fortune when Egypt's then president, Gamal Abdel Nasser, expropriated his cotton trading company in 1964.
Mansour worked as a busboy in a pizza parlor while at North Carolina State University to pay for college.

name: Erik Selin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Erik Selin is CEO of publicly traded real estate firm Fastighets AB Balder, which he founded in 2005.
Selin skipped college to focus on his stock investments but lost it all in the crash of 1987, before moving on to property trades.
At age 24, Selin convinced a local bank to lend him $2 million to finance a deal for a residential development in ?ngelholm, Sweden.
Today 56% of the real estate held by Balder is residential.
Balder also has 50 hotels, making it one of Sweden's largest hotel owners.
forbes_facts: Selin claims to have started reading annual reports at age 12 and trading securities at age 14 with money from summer jobs.
Balder is a partner in a new travel center in Sweden that was supposedly one of the last projects of famed architect Zaha Hadid.

name: Juan Abello
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Juan Abelló's fortune is derived from Torreal, a family-owned global investment firm, which he founded after selling off his family's pharmaceutical assets in the early 1980s.
Established in 1990, Torreal invests broadly across sectors and regions and owns stakes in both public and private companies.
In 2020, Miguel Abelló, Juan's son, was appointed as the executive president of Torreal, while Juan Abelló assumed the role of honorary president.
Abelló has an extensive art collection which includes about 800 works, including those by Rembrandt, Goya, Picasso and Francis Bacon.

name: Catheline Perier D'Ieteren
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Catheline Perier D'Ieteren and her late brother, Roland, are the great great grandchildren of Jean-Joseph D'Ieteren, who founded the D'Ieteren company in 1805.
The Group's portfolio includes five businesses ranging from automobile distribution to real estate and glass repair.
The Group owns D'Ieteren Auto, which exclusively distributes Volkswagen, Audi, Lamborghini, Bugatti and Porsche in Belgium.
The business has been in the family for six generations. Catheline's son, Olivier Perier, is currently deputy chairman.
forbes_facts: The D'Ieteren Gallery in Belgium showcases 200 years of vehicles with D'Ieteren parts, ranging from horse carriages to modern luxury cars.
In 2016 the group acquired the lifestyle brand, Moleskin, in a deal that valued the planner-focused brand at around $572 million.

name: Victor Pinchuk
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Viktor Pinchuk used his Ph.D. in pipe design to found Interpipe, producer of steel products, in 1990.
He still operates Interpipe, which makes pipes and railway wheels, and also Starlight Media, which owns 6 TV stations.
Pinchuk owns Grand Buildings, a landmark historical building on Trafalgar Square in London.
He is a son-in-law of Ukraine's former president Leonid Kuchma.
PinchukArtCenter, which he chairs, is known for its biannual global contemporary art prize, Future Generation Art Prize, which awards $100K to a young artist.
forbes_facts: Pinchuk sponsors an annual event on Ukraine at the World Economic Forum at Davos.

name: Motilal Oswal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Chartered accountant Motilal Oswal cofounded and chairs Mumbai-headquartered Motilal Oswal Financial Services.
From a small stock brooking outfit, Oswal and his billionaire business partner Raamdeo Agrawal, grew it into a financial services firm.
In their early days, the duo would walk a mile from the Bombay Stock Exchange to the nearest payphone to take orders from clients.
Son of a grain trader, Oswal was the first person in his family to go to college.
In 2023, he and cofounder Agrawal pledged to donate 5% of their respective holdings in Motilal Oswal for philanthropic causes such as education, health and rural upliftment.
forbes_facts: When he was starting out, Oswal was turned down by 60 accountancy firms because he couldn't speak English fluently.
Oswal is the chairman of the Jain International Trade Organisation.

name: Saeed Bin Butti Al Qebaisi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2019); Forbes annual (2018-2019)
forbes_bio: Saeed Bin Butti Al Qebaisi is chairman of Centurion Investments, an Abu Dhabi firm with investments in healthcare, money exchange and retail.
Al Qebaisi's most valuable stake is in NMC Health, a London-listed firm that bills itself as the largest private healthcare provider in the U.A.E.
NMC  Healthcare, which runs hospitals and clinics in a dozen countries, was founded by fellow billionaire B.R. Shetty.
He has investment partnerships with Khalifa Bin Butti Al Muhairi, also a billionaire, that include joint stakes in Travelex and UAE Exchange.
forbes_facts: Bin Butti Al Qebaisi comes from a prominent Emirati family that is related by marriage to the royal family of Abu Dhabi.

name: Scot French
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Scot French is a founding partner of HPS Investment Partners, one of the world's biggest alternative credit managers with $149 billion in assets.
French cofounded HPS in 2007 with Scott Kapnick and Michael Patterson, who are both also billionaires.
HPS was sold to BlackRock in July 2025 for around $12 billion in BlackRock stock.
French previously managed a proprietary investment fund within Citigroup, and before that worked at Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers.
He began his career as an accountant at Price Waterhouse after graduating from the University of Illinois.

name: Liu Yachao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2020-2021); Hurun Global (2020-2021); Hurun China (2016-2020); Hurun Global U40 (2020-2021); Hurun China U40 (2019-2020); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Liu Yachao is Chief Operating Officer and a board member at TAL Education Group, one of China's largest education companies.
Liu received an undergraduate degree in mechanics from Peking University in 2003.
He also holds a Ph.D. from the Institute of Mechanics at the Chinese Academy of Science in 2008.
TAL stands for "Tomorrow Advancing Life."
